mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets the model invent an Operation whose (role, kind) is not in the matrix yet outcome=Allowed — a direct LeastPrivilege violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Allowed and op.caller.role = Customer and op.kind = PostClaim }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets an unauthenticated Operation be Allowed, which is exactly what the FR-001 auth-required invariant forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthRequiredViolation { some op: Operation | op.authenticated = False and op.outcome = Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact permits two distinct ApplicationEvents on the same application with identical (prev, new) — the duplicate-audit-entry violation the append-only / one-event-per-change invariants exist to rule out.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some a: LoanApplication | some disj e1, e2: a.events | e1.prevStatus = Submitted and e2.prevStatus = Submitted and e1.newStatus = UnderReview and e2.newStatus = UnderReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets a Decision exist whose decidedBy is some other user, not the application's assigned officer — exactly the FR-013 violation (an unassigned officer somehow recording the decision).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OnlyAssignedDecidesViolation { some d: Decision | d.decidedBy != d.app.assignedOfficer }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets a customer-role Operation expose an officer identity via revealsOfficer — the FR-021 information-leak the scrub_for_role layer is supposed to prevent.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OfficerHiddenViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = Customer and some op.revealsOfficer }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets a customer GetApplicationById succeed on an application owned by a different customer — the cross-tenant read FR-020 prohibits, also breaking the no-leakage invariant (the existence of another customer's application becomes observable).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CustomerOwnershipViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Allowed and op.caller.role = Customer and op.kind = GetApplicationById and some op.target and op.target.customer != op.caller }
